title: Applications of sequence and series in daily life
competency: Solve real-life problems with arithmetic and geometric sequences and series.

keywords.def: A sequence where each term is the previous term plus a fixed number.
The fixed number r: r = next term ÷ this term.
A sum a₁ + a₂ + a₃ + … that never ends.

en.text: A fixed raise, a fixed extra amount each day, or a pattern that grows by the same number is arithmetic. Use Aₙ for one value (the 10th salary) and Sₙ for a total (pay over 12 months). If n is unknown, Sₙ = total gives a quadratic; keep only the positive whole-number root.

am.text: ቋሚ የደሞዝ ጭማሪ ወይም በየቀኑ ቋሚ ተጨማሪ አሪትሜቲክ ነው። ለአንድ እሴት Aₙ፣ ለድምር Sₙ እንጠቀማለን።

screens.title: A rising salary
screens.ask: A salary starts at 5200 ETB a month and rises 320 ETB every month. What is it in month 10?
screens.after: A₁₀ = 5200 + 9 × 320 = 8080 ETB. Nine raises, not ten.

screens.title: Applications of sequences and series
paras: Many real problems are arithmetic or geometric sequences.
Ask: is the same amount added each time? Then it is arithmetic.
One value → use Aₙ.  A total → use Sₙ.

en.text: When a quantity changes by the same percentage each period, multiply by (1 + rate) for growth or (1 − rate) for loss. After n periods: amount × (1 ± rate)ⁿ. Interest, population growth, depreciation and radioactive decay all work this way.

am.text: አንድ መጠን በየጊዜው በአንድ መቶኛ ሲለወጥ ለዕድገት በ (1 + ምጣኔ) ለቅናሽ በ (1 − ምጣኔ) እናባዛለን። ከ n ጊዜ በኋላ፡ መጠን × (1 ± ምጣኔ)ⁿ።

screens.title: Interest on a deposit
screens.ask: Birr 3 500 earns 6% interest a year. How much is in the account after 1 year?
screens.after: 6% of 3 500 is 210, so 3 710 = 3 500 × 1.06. Each year multiplies by 1.06.

screens.title: Why the amounts are geometric
steps: The ratio of neighbours is always 1.06.
So the amounts form a geometric sequence.

ideas.name: Totals that never pass a limit

en.text: If each new amount is a fixed fraction of the last, the total is an infinite geometric series. Its sum G₁/(1 − r) is the limit the total approaches but never passes, like a flower whose growth halves each year or nested squares whose areas halve.

am.text: እያንዳንዱ አዲስ መጠን የቀደመው ቋሚ ክፍልፋይ ከሆነ ድምሩ ኢውሱን ጂኦሜትሪክ ተከታታይ ነው። G₁/(1 − r) ድምሩ የማያልፈው ወሰን ነው።

screens.title: A flower that slows down
screens.ask: A 110 cm flower grows 10 cm in year 1, then half as much each year. Can it reach 140 cm?
screens.after: Growth 10 + 5 + 2.5 + … has sum 10/(1 − 1/2) = 20. So the height stays below 110 + 20 = 130 cm.

screens.title: A limit for the total
paras: Every partial sum is less than 20, so the height never passes 130 cm.

steps: Drop from h. Each bounce reaches r × the last height.

screens.ask: A ball dropped from 10 m rebounds to 50% of its height each time. Total distance = ___ m
Equilateral triangles: each side is the height of the one before. The first has side 2. The total area is ___ (as a decimal, 2 places)
screens.why: Areas have r = (√3/2)² = 3/4. First area √3. Total = √3/(1/4) = 4√3 ≈ 6.93.

screens.text: Growth of 6 cm, then 3 cm, then 1.5 cm, … can add up to more than 12 cm.
screens.why: 6/(1 − 1/2) = 12, and every partial sum is less than 12.

notes.text: Exercise 1.22 Q1 is ambiguous: counting the raise at the 3-year mark gives Birr 26 750 (used here); not counting it gives Birr 26 500.
Example 6 b compares total (cumulative) expenses and income and gets n ≈ 30.3; if it means yearly expenses vs yearly grant, expenses are higher from year 16. Example 6 is not used in graded items.
Example 4 uses G₁ = the deposit, so Gₙ is the amount after n − 1 years; Exercise 1.23 Q4 e asks for the amount after n years, 3500(1.06)ⁿ. Lessons say this explicitly.
Exercise 1.25 Q1 says "r %" but the formula needs r as a fraction (60% → 0.6).
Exercise 1.24 Q3 assumes the first prize is the largest (d = −250).
The book uses Figure 1.5 twice (tree, p.35; letter pattern, p.45).
